- A newly saved link starts Unread and Active (appears in All and Unread).
- Marking a link Read removes it from Unread but keeps it in All (now shown Read).
- Marking a Read link Unread returns it to Unread.
- Archiving removes a link from both All and Unread and places it in Archived;
  this is "putting away", NOT deleting.
- Restoring an archived link returns it to the active library, preserving its
  prior Read/Unread state.

Status is changed via clearly labelled buttons on each entry — "Mark read",
"Mark unread", "Archive", "Restore". This labelled-button style was chosen by
the client over (A) a status pill/menu and (C) a checkbox-plus-icon, because the
labels make each action immediately understandable and archiving is not confused
with reading state.

## Gherkin

Feature: Reading state and archiving

  Background:
    Given read state (Unread/Read) and archive state (Active/Archived) are independent

  Scenario: New link starts unread and active
    When the client saves a new link
    Then it is Unread and Active
    And it appears in the All view and the Unread view

  Scenario: Mark a link read
    Given an Active Unread link
    When the client marks it Read
    Then it no longer appears in the Unread view
    And it still appears in the All view, shown as Read

  Scenario: Mark a read link unread again
    Given an Active Read link
    When the client marks it Unread
    Then it appears in the Unread view again

  Scenario: Archive a link
    Given an Active link (Read or Unread)
    When the client archives it
    Then it no longer appears in the All or Unread views
    And it appears in the Archived view
    And it is not deleted

  Scenario: Restore an archived link preserves reading state
    Given an Archived link that was <priorState> before archiving
    When the client restores it
    Then it returns to the active library
    And its reading state is still <priorState>
    Examples:
      | priorState |
      | Unread     |
      | Read       |

## Assumptions

- View names: All, Unread, Archived. Reading label: "Read" / "Unread"
  (client confirmed these read correctly).
- Read items in All are visually de-emphasised (slight dimming) — client
  approved as helpful.
- Archived items are retained indefinitely until restored (deletion is a
  separate, not-yet-explored action).

## Related scenarios
- SCN-001 (quick save), SCN-002 (duplicate handling)
- Future: permanent deletion (distinct from archiving) — not yet explored.

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Experiment scope

This trial performs the first cycle through acceptance of the implemented
software. Record requests for later cycles without starting another cycle in
this trial.

Requirement exploration takes place in Phase 1. The requirement scenarios
approved in that phase are the baseline for implementation, verification, and
acceptance. During acceptance, an implementation that fails to satisfy an
approved scenario is corrected within the current cycle. A request that changes
an approved scenario or adds a scenario is recorded for a later cycle.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

## Current state

- Current cycle: [1]
- Current Phase: [Phase 1]
- Current step: [SbE reaction loop]
- Approved scenarios: [2]

## File conventions

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)
- Artifact locations:
  - Goal statement: context/goals.md
  - Scenarios: context/scenarios/SCN-NNN.md
  - Scenario index: context/scenarios-index.md
  - Non-functional backlog: context/non-functional-backlog.md
  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
  Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
  scenarios' GWT specifications.
- Do not handle assumptions implicitly
- Do not ask the client questions in technical terms
- Do not show GWT/Gherkin to the client
- During Phase 1, do not hand over a whole prototype and say "take a look"
- Do not enumerate interaction options as text
- Do not ask the client to perform management actions
- Do not propose the Phase 2 switch without edge-case exploration

## Runtime presentation environment

The client reviews artifacts through a separate container. For a runnable web
application, configure its HTTP server to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Use port `4000` for the final application and port `4001` for an HTTP
prototype. The client reaches these at `http://maker:4000` and
`http://maker:4001` on the shared Docker network. Do not give the client
`localhost` or a container IP. The VM capture uses the corresponding
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` address; these addresses serve different callers.

Once the application is ready for review, write `/work/.harness/app.json`:

```json
{"kind": "application", "port": 4000, "path": "/", "start_command": ["npm", "start"], "start_cwd": "/work"}
```

Use `kind: application` with port 4000, or `kind: prototype` with port 4001.
Keep the actual entry path and foreground server command current. `start_command`
is an argument array, not a shell command string. Complete dependency installation
and builds first; this command only starts the prepared application. `start_cwd`
defaults to `/work` and must remain below that directory. For example, a static
prototype can use `["python3", "-m", "http.server", "4001", "--bind", "0.0.0.0",
"--directory", "prototypes"]`.

The broker starts the declared command in a detached container process when the
port is not listening, so it survives the end of your model call. A long-running
foreground tool session alone is not sufficient. Logs are in
`/work/.harness/runtime/server.log`; a failed server receives at most one start
attempt per dialogue round. If it fails, inspect and fix the cause before the
next review. Do not rely on this mechanism to implement or repeatedly retry a
failing application until it succeeds.

Mark a visible application element with `data-harness-ready="true"` only after
its initial UI and necessary data have loaded. The same marker applies to a
valid empty state, login page, or static prototype; do not mark a loading/error
placeholder as ready. The harness uses this shared marker instead of a custom
CSS selector. This confirms presentation readiness, not feature correctness.
If startup arguments or built code change, stop your previous application
server before requesting another presentation; an already-running server is
not silently replaced. The prototype and application must not share a port.
When login is required, provide working review credentials or a review entry
path using the actual implementation. Make HTTP-session cookies work in this
review environment; keep production deployment settings separate. Never claim
that a prepared state proves an interaction that was not performed.

Use the entry path and query string that show the state under discussion. For
COSPEC, save any post-action screenshots for the client under `prototypes/` and
name the relevant file in your guidance. Those images are copied with their
relative paths; `/work` itself is not shared with the client.

This is runtime delivery information, not a development method or a requirement
to implement before the client approves your method's relevant review gates.
For standalone COSPEC prototypes, continue using `prototypes/`; their existing
HTML and supporting files are delivered separately.

## Available runtime and verification tools

The shared image provides Node.js 24, npm, Python, a C/C++ build toolchain,
Playwright 1.61.0 for Python and Node, Chromium, and its Linux dependencies.
Use `python` (the image's browser-tools virtual environment) for Python browser
checks, and `playwright` for the installed CLI. Browser binaries are shared at
`/opt/playwright-browsers`. If using Playwright in a project's test imports,
pin `playwright` or `@playwright/test` to `1.61.0` in its development dependencies
so its browser revision matches the installed binaries. Do not download a
second browser version during a trial. Application frameworks and databases
are not prescribed; use compatible dependencies and preserve lockfiles.
Report unavailable external services and unfinished validation honestly.

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Experiment scope

This trial performs the first cycle through acceptance of the implemented
software. Record requests for later cycles without starting another cycle in
this trial.

Requirement exploration takes place in Phase 1. The requirement scenarios
approved in that phase are the baseline for implementation, verification, and
acceptance. During acceptance, an implementation that fails to satisfy an
approved scenario is corrected within the current cycle. A request that changes
an approved scenario or adds a scenario is recorded for a later cycle.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

## Current state

- Current cycle: [1]
- Current Phase: [Phase 1]
- Current step: [SbE reaction loop]
- Approved scenarios: [3]

## File conventions

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)
- Artifact locations:
  - Goal statement: context/goals.md
  - Scenarios: context/scenarios/SCN-NNN.md
  - Scenario index: context/scenarios-index.md
  - Non-functional backlog: context/non-functional-backlog.md
  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
  Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
  scenarios' GWT specifications.
- Do not handle assumptions implicitly
- Do not ask the client questions in technical terms
- Do not show GWT/Gherkin to the client
- During Phase 1, do not hand over a whole prototype and say "take a look"
- Do not enumerate interaction options as text
- Do not ask the client to perform management actions
- Do not propose the Phase 2 switch without edge-case exploration

## Runtime presentation environment

The client reviews artifacts through a separate container. For a runnable web
application, configure its HTTP server to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Use port `4000` for the final application and port `4001` for an HTTP
prototype. The client reaches these at `http://maker:4000` and
`http://maker:4001` on the shared Docker network. Do not give the client
`localhost` or a container IP. The VM capture uses the corresponding
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` address; these addresses serve different callers.

Once the application is ready for review, write `/work/.harness/app.json`:

```json
{"kind": "application", "port": 4000, "path": "/", "start_command": ["npm", "start"], "start_cwd": "/work"}
```

Use `kind: application` with port 4000, or `kind: prototype` with port 4001.
Keep the actual entry path and foreground server command current. `start_command`
is an argument array, not a shell command string. Complete dependency installation
and builds first; this command only starts the prepared application. `start_cwd`
defaults to `/work` and must remain below that directory. For example, a static
prototype can use `["python3", "-m", "http.server", "4001", "--bind", "0.0.0.0",
"--directory", "prototypes"]`.

The broker starts the declared command in a detached container process when the
port is not listening, so it survives the end of your model call. A long-running
foreground tool session alone is not sufficient. Logs are in
`/work/.harness/runtime/server.log`; a failed server receives at most one start
attempt per dialogue round. If it fails, inspect and fix the cause before the
next review. Do not rely on this mechanism to implement or repeatedly retry a
failing application until it succeeds.

Mark a visible application element with `data-harness-ready="true"` only after
its initial UI and necessary data have loaded. The same marker applies to a
valid empty state, login page, or static prototype; do not mark a loading/error
placeholder as ready. The harness uses this shared marker instead of a custom
CSS selector. This confirms presentation readiness, not feature correctness.
If startup arguments or built code change, stop your previous application
server before requesting another presentation; an already-running server is
not silently replaced. The prototype and application must not share a port.
When login is required, provide working review credentials or a review entry
path using the actual implementation. Make HTTP-session cookies work in this
review environment; keep production deployment settings separate. Never claim
that a prepared state proves an interaction that was not performed.

Use the entry path and query string that show the state under discussion. For
COSPEC, save any post-action screenshots for the client under `prototypes/` and
name the relevant file in your guidance. Those images are copied with their
relative paths; `/work` itself is not shared with the client.

This is runtime delivery information, not a development method or a requirement
to implement before the client approves your method's relevant review gates.
For standalone COSPEC prototypes, continue using `prototypes/`; their existing
HTML and supporting files are delivered separately.

## Available runtime and verification tools

The shared image provides Node.js 24, npm, Python, a C/C++ build toolchain,
Playwright 1.61.0 for Python and Node, Chromium, and its Linux dependencies.
Use `python` (the image's browser-tools virtual environment) for Python browser
checks, and `playwright` for the installed CLI. Browser binaries are shared at
`/opt/playwright-browsers`. If using Playwright in a project's test imports,
pin `playwright` or `@playwright/test` to `1.61.0` in its development dependencies
so its browser revision matches the installed binaries. Do not download a
second browser version during a trial. Application frameworks and databases
are not prescribed; use compatible dependencies and preserve lockfiles.
Report unavailable external services and unfinished validation honestly.

Removing a tag: a small "✕" on the chip removes it from that entry.

e.g. filtering "reference" while on Unread shows only unread links tagged
"reference". A small bar shows which tag is active and offers a control to clear

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Experiment scope

This trial performs the first cycle through acceptance of the implemented
software. Record requests for later cycles without starting another cycle in
this trial.

Requirement exploration takes place in Phase 1. The requirement scenarios
approved in that phase are the baseline for implementation, verification, and
acceptance. During acceptance, an implementation that fails to satisfy an
approved scenario is corrected within the current cycle. A request that changes
an approved scenario or adds a scenario is recorded for a later cycle.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

## Current state

- Current cycle: [1]
- Current Phase: [Phase 1]
- Current step: [SbE reaction loop]
- Approved scenarios: [3]

## File conventions

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)
- Artifact locations:
  - Goal statement: context/goals.md
  - Scenarios: context/scenarios/SCN-NNN.md
  - Scenario index: context/scenarios-index.md
  - Non-functional backlog: context/non-functional-backlog.md
  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
  Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
  scenarios' GWT specifications.
- Do not handle assumptions implicitly
- Do not ask the client questions in technical terms
- Do not show GWT/Gherkin to the client
- During Phase 1, do not hand over a whole prototype and say "take a look"
- Do not enumerate interaction options as text
- Do not ask the client to perform management actions
- Do not propose the Phase 2 switch without edge-case exploration

## Runtime presentation environment

The client reviews artifacts through a separate container. For a runnable web
application, configure its HTTP server to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Use port `4000` for the final application and port `4001` for an HTTP
prototype. The client reaches these at `http://maker:4000` and
`http://maker:4001` on the shared Docker network. Do not give the client
`localhost` or a container IP. The VM capture uses the corresponding
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` address; these addresses serve different callers.

Once the application is ready for review, write `/work/.harness/app.json`:

```json
{"kind": "application", "port": 4000, "path": "/", "start_command": ["npm", "start"], "start_cwd": "/work"}
```

Use `kind: application` with port 4000, or `kind: prototype` with port 4001.
Keep the actual entry path and foreground server command current. `start_command`
is an argument array, not a shell command string. Complete dependency installation
and builds first; this command only starts the prepared application. `start_cwd`
defaults to `/work` and must remain below that directory. For example, a static
prototype can use `["python3", "-m", "http.server", "4001", "--bind", "0.0.0.0",
"--directory", "prototypes"]`.

The broker starts the declared command in a detached container process when the
port is not listening, so it survives the end of your model call. A long-running
foreground tool session alone is not sufficient. Logs are in
`/work/.harness/runtime/server.log`; a failed server receives at most one start
attempt per dialogue round. If it fails, inspect and fix the cause before the
next review. Do not rely on this mechanism to implement or repeatedly retry a
failing application until it succeeds.

Mark a visible application element with `data-harness-ready="true"` only after
its initial UI and necessary data have loaded. The same marker applies to a
valid empty state, login page, or static prototype; do not mark a loading/error
placeholder as ready. The harness uses this shared marker instead of a custom
CSS selector. This confirms presentation readiness, not feature correctness.
If startup arguments or built code change, stop your previous application
server before requesting another presentation; an already-running server is
not silently replaced. The prototype and application must not share a port.
When login is required, provide working review credentials or a review entry
path using the actual implementation. Make HTTP-session cookies work in this
review environment; keep production deployment settings separate. Never claim
that a prepared state proves an interaction that was not performed.

Use the entry path and query string that show the state under discussion. For
COSPEC, save any post-action screenshots for the client under `prototypes/` and
name the relevant file in your guidance. Those images are copied with their
relative paths; `/work` itself is not shared with the client.

This is runtime delivery information, not a development method or a requirement
to implement before the client approves your method's relevant review gates.
For standalone COSPEC prototypes, continue using `prototypes/`; their existing
HTML and supporting files are delivered separately.

## Available runtime and verification tools

The shared image provides Node.js 24, npm, Python, a C/C++ build toolchain,
Playwright 1.61.0 for Python and Node, Chromium, and its Linux dependencies.
Use `python` (the image's browser-tools virtual environment) for Python browser
checks, and `playwright` for the installed CLI. Browser binaries are shared at
`/opt/playwright-browsers`. If using Playwright in a project's test imports,
pin `playwright` or `@playwright/test` to `1.61.0` in its development dependencies
so its browser revision matches the installed binaries. Do not download a
second browser version during a trial. Application frameworks and databases
are not prescribed; use compatible dependencies and preserve lockfiles.
Report unavailable external services and unfinished validation honestly.

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Experiment scope

This trial performs the first cycle through acceptance of the implemented
software. Record requests for later cycles without starting another cycle in
this trial.

Requirement exploration takes place in Phase 1. The requirement scenarios
approved in that phase are the baseline for implementation, verification, and
acceptance. During acceptance, an implementation that fails to satisfy an
approved scenario is corrected within the current cycle. A request that changes
an approved scenario or adds a scenario is recorded for a later cycle.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

## Current state

- Current cycle: [1]
- Current Phase: [Phase 1]
- Current step: [SbE reaction loop]
- Approved scenarios: [4]

## File conventions

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)
- Artifact locations:
  - Goal statement: context/goals.md
  - Scenarios: context/scenarios/SCN-NNN.md
  - Scenario index: context/scenarios-index.md
  - Non-functional backlog: context/non-functional-backlog.md
  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
  Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
  scenarios' GWT specifications.
- Do not handle assumptions implicitly
- Do not ask the client questions in technical terms
- Do not show GWT/Gherkin to the client
- During Phase 1, do not hand over a whole prototype and say "take a look"
- Do not enumerate interaction options as text
- Do not ask the client to perform management actions
- Do not propose the Phase 2 switch without edge-case exploration

## Runtime presentation environment

The client reviews artifacts through a separate container. For a runnable web
application, configure its HTTP server to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Use port `4000` for the final application and port `4001` for an HTTP
prototype. The client reaches these at `http://maker:4000` and
`http://maker:4001` on the shared Docker network. Do not give the client
`localhost` or a container IP. The VM capture uses the corresponding
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` address; these addresses serve different callers.

Once the application is ready for review, write `/work/.harness/app.json`:

```json
{"kind": "application", "port": 4000, "path": "/", "start_command": ["npm", "start"], "start_cwd": "/work"}
```

Use `kind: application` with port 4000, or `kind: prototype` with port 4001.
Keep the actual entry path and foreground server command current. `start_command`
is an argument array, not a shell command string. Complete dependency installation
and builds first; this command only starts the prepared application. `start_cwd`
defaults to `/work` and must remain below that directory. For example, a static
prototype can use `["python3", "-m", "http.server", "4001", "--bind", "0.0.0.0",
"--directory", "prototypes"]`.

The broker starts the declared command in a detached container process when the
port is not listening, so it survives the end of your model call. A long-running
foreground tool session alone is not sufficient. Logs are in
`/work/.harness/runtime/server.log`; a failed server receives at most one start
attempt per dialogue round. If it fails, inspect and fix the cause before the
next review. Do not rely on this mechanism to implement or repeatedly retry a
failing application until it succeeds.

Mark a visible application element with `data-harness-ready="true"` only after
its initial UI and necessary data have loaded. The same marker applies to a
valid empty state, login page, or static prototype; do not mark a loading/error
placeholder as ready. The harness uses this shared marker instead of a custom
CSS selector. This confirms presentation readiness, not feature correctness.
If startup arguments or built code change, stop your previous application
server before requesting another presentation; an already-running server is
not silently replaced. The prototype and application must not share a port.
When login is required, provide working review credentials or a review entry
path using the actual implementation. Make HTTP-session cookies work in this
review environment; keep production deployment settings separate. Never claim
that a prepared state proves an interaction that was not performed.

Use the entry path and query string that show the state under discussion. For
COSPEC, save any post-action screenshots for the client under `prototypes/` and
name the relevant file in your guidance. Those images are copied with their
relative paths; `/work` itself is not shared with the client.

This is runtime delivery information, not a development method or a requirement
to implement before the client approves your method's relevant review gates.
For standalone COSPEC prototypes, continue using `prototypes/`; their existing
HTML and supporting files are delivered separately.

## Available runtime and verification tools

The shared image provides Node.js 24, npm, Python, a C/C++ build toolchain,
Playwright 1.61.0 for Python and Node, Chromium, and its Linux dependencies.
Use `python` (the image's browser-tools virtual environment) for Python browser
checks, and `playwright` for the installed CLI. Browser binaries are shared at
`/opt/playwright-browsers`. If using Playwright in a project's test imports,
pin `playwright` or `@playwright/test` to `1.61.0` in its development dependencies
so its browser revision matches the installed binaries. Do not download a
second browser version during a trial. Application frameworks and databases
are not prescribed; use compatible dependencies and preserve lockfiles.
Report unavailable external services and unfinished validation honestly.

input.content:
Scenario ID: SCN-005
Title: Narrow by several tags at once (match all selected)
Type: Happy Path
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-001
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour

The tag filter accepts more than one tag at a time. When several tags are
selected, the list shows only links that carry ALL of the selected tags (AND).
Each additional selected tag narrows the list further.

- Clicking an unselected tag adds it to the filter; clicking a selected
  (highlighted) tag again removes it.
- Selected tags are highlighted on the entries and listed in the filter bar,
  where each can be removed individually via its "✕".
- "Clear tag filter" removes all selected tags at once.
- The multi-tag filter still applies within the current view (All / Unread /
  Archived), consistent with SCN-004.

The client confirmed "match all" is the intended behaviour and that removing
filters individually, toggling a tag off, and clearing all feel straightforward.

## Gherkin

Feature: Filter by multiple tags (match all)

  Scenario: Combining tags narrows to links carrying all of them
    Given links exist with various tags in the current view
    When the client selects tag A
    Then only links tagged A are shown
    When the client also selects tag B
    Then only links tagged with both A and B are shown

  Scenario: Remove one tag from a multi-tag filter
    Given the filter has tags A and B selected
    When the client removes tag B
    Then the list shows links tagged A again

  Scenario: Toggling a selected tag off
    Given tag A is selected
    When the client clicks tag A again
    Then tag A is removed from the filter

  Scenario: Clear all tag filters
    Given one or more tags are selected
    When the client chooses "Clear tag filter"
    Then no tag filter is applied and the full current view is shown

## Assumptions

- Combination semantics = AND (match all). OR / "any of" was not requested.
- Selection is case-insensitive, consistent with SCN-004.

## Related scenarios
- SCN-004 (tags: chips, add/remove, single-tag filter within a view)

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Experiment scope

This trial performs the first cycle through acceptance of the implemented
software. Record requests for later cycles without starting another cycle in
this trial.

Requirement exploration takes place in Phase 1. The requirement scenarios
approved in that phase are the baseline for implementation, verification, and
acceptance. During acceptance, an implementation that fails to satisfy an
approved scenario is corrected within the current cycle. A request that changes
an approved scenario or adds a scenario is recorded for a later cycle.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

## Current state

- Current cycle: [1]
- Current Phase: [Phase 1]
- Current step: [SbE reaction loop]
- Approved scenarios: [4]

## File conventions

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)
- Artifact locations:
  - Goal statement: context/goals.md
  - Scenarios: context/scenarios/SCN-NNN.md
  - Scenario index: context/scenarios-index.md
  - Non-functional backlog: context/non-functional-backlog.md
  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
  Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
  scenarios' GWT specifications.
- Do not handle assumptions implicitly
- Do not ask the client questions in technical terms
- Do not show GWT/Gherkin to the client
- During Phase 1, do not hand over a whole prototype and say "take a look"
- Do not enumerate interaction options as text
- Do not ask the client to perform management actions
- Do not propose the Phase 2 switch without edge-case exploration

## Runtime presentation environment

The client reviews artifacts through a separate container. For a runnable web
application, configure its HTTP server to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Use port `4000` for the final application and port `4001` for an HTTP
prototype. The client reaches these at `http://maker:4000` and
`http://maker:4001` on the shared Docker network. Do not give the client
`localhost` or a container IP. The VM capture uses the corresponding
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` address; these addresses serve different callers.

Once the application is ready for review, write `/work/.harness/app.json`:

```json
{"kind": "application", "port": 4000, "path": "/", "start_command": ["npm", "start"], "start_cwd": "/work"}
```

Use `kind: application` with port 4000, or `kind: prototype` with port 4001.
Keep the actual entry path and foreground server command current. `start_command`
is an argument array, not a shell command string. Complete dependency installation
and builds first; this command only starts the prepared application. `start_cwd`
defaults to `/work` and must remain below that directory. For example, a static
prototype can use `["python3", "-m", "http.server", "4001", "--bind", "0.0.0.0",
"--directory", "prototypes"]`.

The broker starts the declared command in a detached container process when the
port is not listening, so it survives the end of your model call. A long-running
foreground tool session alone is not sufficient. Logs are in
`/work/.harness/runtime/server.log`; a failed server receives at most one start
attempt per dialogue round. If it fails, inspect and fix the cause before the
next review. Do not rely on this mechanism to implement or repeatedly retry a
failing application until it succeeds.

Mark a visible application element with `data-harness-ready="true"` only after
its initial UI and necessary data have loaded. The same marker applies to a
valid empty state, login page, or static prototype; do not mark a loading/error
placeholder as ready. The harness uses this shared marker instead of a custom
CSS selector. This confirms presentation readiness, not feature correctness.
If startup arguments or built code change, stop your previous application
server before requesting another presentation; an already-running server is
not silently replaced. The prototype and application must not share a port.
When login is required, provide working review credentials or a review entry
path using the actual implementation. Make HTTP-session cookies work in this
review environment; keep production deployment settings separate. Never claim
that a prepared state proves an interaction that was not performed.

Use the entry path and query string that show the state under discussion. For
COSPEC, save any post-action screenshots for the client under `prototypes/` and
name the relevant file in your guidance. Those images are copied with their
relative paths; `/work` itself is not shared with the client.

This is runtime delivery information, not a development method or a requirement
to implement before the client approves your method's relevant review gates.
For standalone COSPEC prototypes, continue using `prototypes/`; their existing
HTML and supporting files are delivered separately.

## Available runtime and verification tools

The shared image provides Node.js 24, npm, Python, a C/C++ build toolchain,
Playwright 1.61.0 for Python and Node, Chromium, and its Linux dependencies.
Use `python` (the image's browser-tools virtual environment) for Python browser
checks, and `playwright` for the installed CLI. Browser binaries are shared at
`/opt/playwright-browsers`. If using Playwright in a project's test imports,
pin `playwright` or `@playwright/test` to `1.61.0` in its development dependencies
so its browser revision matches the installed binaries. Do not download a
second browser version during a trial. Application frameworks and databases
are not prescribed; use compatible dependencies and preserve lockfiles.
Report unavailable external services and unfinished validation honestly.

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Experiment scope

This trial performs the first cycle through acceptance of the implemented
software. Record requests for later cycles without starting another cycle in
this trial.

Requirement exploration takes place in Phase 1. The requirement scenarios
approved in that phase are the baseline for implementation, verification, and
acceptance. During acceptance, an implementation that fails to satisfy an
approved scenario is corrected within the current cycle. A request that changes
an approved scenario or adds a scenario is recorded for a later cycle.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

## Current state

- Current cycle: [1]
- Current Phase: [Phase 1]
- Current step: [SbE reaction loop]
- Approved scenarios: [5]

## File conventions

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)
- Artifact locations:
  - Goal statement: context/goals.md
  - Scenarios: context/scenarios/SCN-NNN.md
  - Scenario index: context/scenarios-index.md
  - Non-functional backlog: context/non-functional-backlog.md
  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
  Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
  scenarios' GWT specifications.
- Do not handle assumptions implicitly
- Do not ask the client questions in technical terms
- Do not show GWT/Gherkin to the client
- During Phase 1, do not hand over a whole prototype and say "take a look"
- Do not enumerate interaction options as text
- Do not ask the client to perform management actions
- Do not propose the Phase 2 switch without edge-case exploration

## Runtime presentation environment

The client reviews artifacts through a separate container. For a runnable web
application, configure its HTTP server to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Use port `4000` for the final application and port `4001` for an HTTP
prototype. The client reaches these at `http://maker:4000` and
`http://maker:4001` on the shared Docker network. Do not give the client
`localhost` or a container IP. The VM capture uses the corresponding
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` address; these addresses serve different callers.

**2. Formatted notes.** In that review panel's note field (or later via **✏ Edit**), try typing formatting — for example:
```
# My heading
Some **bold** text and a [link](https://example.org)

```
When you save and view the entry, that renders as a real heading, bold text, a clickable link, and a bulleted list. A small hint under the field shows the formatting you can use.

**3. Edit the address itself.** Open **✏ Edit** on any entry — there's now an **Address** field at the top. Change it and save. If you change it to an address you've *already* saved elsewhere, you'll get a clear message ("*already saved as …*") and nothing is changed. Change it to a genuinely new address and the entry updates.

Three choices I made, for your judgment:

- **Saving now has that extra review step** — a small trade of speed for the chance to fix details up front. Does that feel worth it, or too heavy for a quick save?
- **Notes use simple Markdown-style marks** (`**bold**`, `# heading`, `- list`, `[text](url)`). Is that the kind of "simple formatting" you meant?

Scenario ID: SCN-007
Title: Review and correct auto-filled details before finalizing a save
Type: Happy Path
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-001
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour

Saving a link is a brief two-step flow: fetch, then review, then add.

When the client enters an address and presses Save, the system fetches the
page's details and shows a review panel pre-filled with the auto-filled Title
and Description (both editable), the address, and an optional note field. The
client can correct the details, then press "Add to library" to finalize, or
"Discard" to back out without saving anything.

- If the fetched page details could not be read, the review panel says so and
  invites the client to fill them in.
- If the address is already saved (SCN-002 identity), no review is shown; the
  client is taken to the existing entry instead.
- The entry is created only when the client confirms "Add to library"; it then
  appears at the top of the list, briefly highlighted (SCN-001).

The client approved the review step as worth the small extra effort: it is still
quick and prevents poor auto-filled details from becoming something to fix later.
"Discard" makes backing out clear.

## Gherkin

Feature: Review before finalizing a save

  Scenario: Review and correct then add
    Given the client enters a new address and presses Save
    Then a review panel shows the auto-filled title and description, editable
    When the client adjusts them and chooses "Add to library"
    Then a new entry is created with the reviewed details and appears at the top

  Scenario: Discard a pending save
    Given the review panel is shown for a fetched address
    When the client chooses "Discard"
    Then no entry is created

  Scenario: Details could not be fetched
    Given the client saves an address whose page details cannot be read
    Then the review panel indicates this and lets the client fill in the details

  Scenario: Address already saved skips review
    Given the address is already in the library
    When the client presses Save
    Then no review panel is shown
    And the client is taken to the existing entry (SCN-002)

## Assumptions

- Review fields = title, description, optional note. Tags are added after saving
  (SCN-004), not in the review step.
- This refines the finalization of SCN-001: the recognizable entry now appears
  upon "Add to library" rather than immediately on Save.

## Related scenarios
- SCN-001 (quick save / auto-fill), SCN-002 (duplicate), SCN-006 (editing)

Scenario ID: SCN-001
Title: Quick-save a link and see it become a recognizable entry
Type: Happy Path
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-001
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour

The client pastes a link's address into a single save box pinned at the top of
the page and presses Save. The system automatically retrieves recognizable
details about the page and creates a saved entry. The new entry appears at the
top of a readable list (newest first) and is briefly highlighted.

Each entry shows, so the link is recognizable at a glance:
- the page title
- a short description of the page
- the site it came from
- the site icon (favicon)
- how long ago it was saved

A plain address without the leading protocol (e.g. "example.com") is accepted
and understood. When page details cannot be retrieved, the entry is still
created using the address, with a gentle note that details couldn't be fetched.

The client confirmed: the set of details shown is right, the calm layout with a
pinned save box and newest-first ordering is right, and saving via a single
address field plus a Save button is the quick-saving experience intended.

## Gherkin

Feature: Save a link to the library

    Given the library is open
    When the client enters a link address and presses Save
    Then the system retrieves the page's title, description, site name, and icon
    And a new entry showing those details and the time saved appears at the top
      of the list
    And the new entry is briefly highlighted

    Given the library is open

    When the client saves a link whose page cannot be read for details
    Then an entry is still created using the address
    And the entry carries a gentle note that details couldn't be fetched

    Given the library is open
    When the client presses Save with no address entered
    Then no entry is created

## Assumptions

- Entry ordering is newest-first (client confirmed).

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Experiment scope

This trial performs the first cycle through acceptance of the implemented
software. Record requests for later cycles without starting another cycle in
this trial.

Requirement exploration takes place in Phase 1. The requirement scenarios
approved in that phase are the baseline for implementation, verification, and
acceptance. During acceptance, an implementation that fails to satisfy an
approved scenario is corrected within the current cycle. A request that changes
an approved scenario or adds a scenario is recorded for a later cycle.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
  Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
  scenarios' GWT specifications.
- Do not handle assumptions implicitly
- Do not ask the client questions in technical terms
- Do not show GWT/Gherkin to the client
- During Phase 1, do not hand over a whole prototype and say "take a look"
- Do not enumerate interaction options as text
- Do not ask the client to perform management actions
- Do not propose the Phase 2 switch without edge-case exploration

## Runtime presentation environment

The client reviews artifacts through a separate container. For a runnable web
application, configure its HTTP server to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Use port `4000` for the final application and port `4001` for an HTTP
prototype. The client reaches these at `http://maker:4000` and
`http://maker:4001` on the shared Docker network. Do not give the client
`localhost` or a container IP. The VM capture uses the corresponding
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` address; these addresses serve different callers.

Once the application is ready for review, write `/work/.harness/app.json`:

```json
{"kind": "application", "port": 4000, "path": "/", "start_command": ["npm", "start"], "start_cwd": "/work"}
```

Use `kind: application` with port 4000, or `kind: prototype` with port 4001.
Keep the actual entry path and foreground server command current. `start_command`
is an argument array, not a shell command string. Complete dependency installation
and builds first; this command only starts the prepared application. `start_cwd`
defaults to `/work` and must remain below that directory. For example, a static
prototype can use `["python3", "-m", "http.server", "4001", "--bind", "0.0.0.0",
"--directory", "prototypes"]`.

The broker starts the declared command in a detached container process when the
port is not listening, so it survives the end of your model call. A long-running
foreground tool session alone is not sufficient. Logs are in
`/work/.harness/runtime/server.log`; a failed server receives at most one start
attempt per dialogue round. If it fails, inspect and fix the cause before the
next review. Do not rely on this mechanism to implement or repeatedly retry a
failing application until it succeeds.

Mark a visible application element with `data-harness-ready="true"` only after
its initial UI and necessary data have loaded. The same marker applies to a
valid empty state, login page, or static prototype; do not mark a loading/error
placeholder as ready. The harness uses this shared marker instead of a custom
CSS selector. This confirms presentation readiness, not feature correctness.
If startup arguments or built code change, stop your previous application
server before requesting another presentation; an already-running server is
not silently replaced. The prototype and application must not share a port.
When login is required, provide working review credentials or a review entry
path using the actual implementation. Make HTTP-session cookies work in this
review environment; keep production deployment settings separate. Never claim
that a prepared state proves an interaction that was not performed.

Use the entry path and query string that show the state under discussion. For
COSPEC, save any post-action screenshots for the client under `prototypes/` and
name the relevant file in your guidance. Those images are copied with their
relative paths; `/work` itself is not shared with the client.

This is runtime delivery information, not a development method or a requirement
to implement before the client approves your method's relevant review gates.
For standalone COSPEC prototypes, continue using `prototypes/`; their existing
HTML and supporting files are delivered separately.

## Available runtime and verification tools

The shared image provides Node.js 24, npm, Python, a C/C++ build toolchain,
Playwright 1.61.0 for Python and Node, Chromium, and its Linux dependencies.
Use `python` (the image's browser-tools virtual environment) for Python browser
checks, and `playwright` for the installed CLI. Browser binaries are shared at
`/opt/playwright-browsers`. If using Playwright in a project's test imports,
pin `playwright` or `@playwright/test` to `1.61.0` in its development dependencies
so its browser revision matches the installed binaries. Do not download a
second browser version during a trial. Application frameworks and databases
are not prescribed; use compatible dependencies and preserve lockfiles.
Report unavailable external services and unfinished validation honestly.

For “strong search,” I also expect:

- `#reference` to search specifically for that tag.
- Quotation marks to find an exact phrase, such as `"progressive disclosure"`.
- `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, and parentheses for more precise searches, such as `rome (#article OR #book)`.
- Those operator words to be treated as operators unless quoted when I genuinely want to search for the word itself.

Please add those behaviors before I approve search.

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Experiment scope

This trial performs the first cycle through acceptance of the implemented
software. Record requests for later cycles without starting another cycle in
this trial.

Requirement exploration takes place in Phase 1. The requirement scenarios
approved in that phase are the baseline for implementation, verification, and
acceptance. During acceptance, an implementation that fails to satisfy an
approved scenario is corrected within the current cycle. A request that changes
an approved scenario or adds a scenario is recorded for a later cycle.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

## Current state

- Current cycle: [1]
- Current Phase: [Phase 1]
- Current step: [SbE reaction loop]
- Approved scenarios: [7]

## File conventions

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)
- Artifact locations:
  - Goal statement: context/goals.md
  - Scenarios: context/scenarios/SCN-NNN.md
  - Scenario index: context/scenarios-index.md
  - Non-functional backlog: context/non-functional-backlog.md
  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
  Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
  scenarios' GWT specifications.
- Do not handle assumptions implicitly
- Do not ask the client questions in technical terms
- Do not show GWT/Gherkin to the client
- During Phase 1, do not hand over a whole prototype and say "take a look"
- Do not enumerate interaction options as text
- Do not ask the client to perform management actions
- Do not propose the Phase 2 switch without edge-case exploration

## Runtime presentation environment

The client reviews artifacts through a separate container. For a runnable web
application, configure its HTTP server to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Use port `4000` for the final application and port `4001` for an HTTP
prototype. The client reaches these at `http://maker:4000` and
`http://maker:4001` on the shared Docker network. Do not give the client
`localhost` or a container IP. The VM capture uses the corresponding
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` address; these addresses serve different callers.

Once the application is ready for review, write `/work/.harness/app.json`:

```json
{"kind": "application", "port": 4000, "path": "/", "start_command": ["npm", "start"], "start_cwd": "/work"}
```

Use `kind: application` with port 4000, or `kind: prototype` with port 4001.
Keep the actual entry path and foreground server command current. `start_command`
is an argument array, not a shell command string. Complete dependency installation
and builds first; this command only starts the prepared application. `start_cwd`
defaults to `/work` and must remain below that directory. For example, a static
prototype can use `["python3", "-m", "http.server", "4001", "--bind", "0.0.0.0",
"--directory", "prototypes"]`.

The broker starts the declared command in a detached container process when the
port is not listening, so it survives the end of your model call. A long-running
foreground tool session alone is not sufficient. Logs are in
`/work/.harness/runtime/server.log`; a failed server receives at most one start
attempt per dialogue round. If it fails, inspect and fix the cause before the
next review. Do not rely on this mechanism to implement or repeatedly retry a
failing application until it succeeds.

Mark a visible application element with `data-harness-ready="true"` only after
its initial UI and necessary data have loaded. The same marker applies to a
valid empty state, login page, or static prototype; do not mark a loading/error
placeholder as ready. The harness uses this shared marker instead of a custom
CSS selector. This confirms presentation readiness, not feature correctness.
If startup arguments or built code change, stop your previous application
server before requesting another presentation; an already-running server is
not silently replaced. The prototype and application must not share a port.
When login is required, provide working review credentials or a review entry
path using the actual implementation. Make HTTP-session cookies work in this
review environment; keep production deployment settings separate. Never claim
that a prepared state proves an interaction that was not performed.

Use the entry path and query string that show the state under discussion. For
COSPEC, save any post-action screenshots for the client under `prototypes/` and
name the relevant file in your guidance. Those images are copied with their
relative paths; `/work` itself is not shared with the client.

This is runtime delivery information, not a development method or a requirement
to implement before the client approves your method's relevant review gates.
For standalone COSPEC prototypes, continue using `prototypes/`; their existing
HTML and supporting files are delivered separately.

## Available runtime and verification tools

The shared image provides Node.js 24, npm, Python, a C/C++ build toolchain,
Playwright 1.61.0 for Python and Node, Chromium, and its Linux dependencies.
Use `python` (the image's browser-tools virtual environment) for Python browser
checks, and `playwright` for the installed CLI. Browser binaries are shared at
`/opt/playwright-browsers`. If using Playwright in a project's test imports,
pin `playwright` or `@playwright/test` to `1.61.0` in its development dependencies
so its browser revision matches the installed binaries. Do not download a
second browser version during a trial. Application frameworks and databases
are not prescribed; use compatible dependencies and preserve lockfiles.
Report unavailable external services and unfinished validation honestly.

Scenario ID: SCN-008
Title: Strong search within the current view, with a query language
Type: Happy Path
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-001
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour

A search box searches the client's links and shows a result count.

Scope: search runs WITHIN the current view (All / Unread / Archived). Archived
links are excluded from an All or Unread search because they are intentionally
put away; they surface only when searching from the Archived view. Switching
views re-runs the same query in the new view's scope — it does not discard the
search.

Fields searched (for ordinary text): title, description, tags, note, site name,
and address.

Query language:
- Ordinary words: case-insensitive; several words must ALL match (implicit AND).
- "exact phrase": text in quotes matches as a contiguous phrase.
- #tag: matches a link carrying that tag EXACTLY (whole tag, case-insensitive) —
  not the same as the word appearing in text.
- Boolean operators AND, OR, NOT and parentheses for grouping, e.g.
  rome (#article OR #book). Precedence: NOT binds tightest, then AND, then OR;
  parentheses override.
- The operator words AND/OR/NOT are treated as operators when unquoted; to search
  for one of these as a literal word, put it in quotes (e.g. "and").

Matches of ordinary text terms are highlighted in the results. Clearing the box
(✕) or having an empty box returns to the normal view.

The client approved all of the above, confirming exact-tag matching (partial tag
matching could surprise) and the operator precedence.

## Gherkin

Feature: Search the library

  Scenario: Search is scoped to the current view
    Given a link is archived
    When the client searches for one of its words from the All view
    Then it does not appear
    When the client switches to the Archived view with the same query
    Then it appears

  Scenario: Switching views keeps the query
    Given a search query is entered
    When the client switches view
    Then the same query is applied within the new view

  Scenario: Ordinary multi-word search matches all words
    When the client searches "css layout"
    Then only links containing both words (in any searched field) match

  Scenario: Exact phrase
    When the client searches "progressive disclosure" in quotes
    Then only links containing that contiguous phrase match

  Scenario: Tag token matches a whole tag
    When the client searches #reference
    Then only links carrying the tag "reference" match

  Scenario: Boolean operators and grouping
    When the client searches web AND (css OR ux)
    Then links matching web and (css or ux) match, per NOT>AND>OR precedence

  Scenario: Operator word as a literal
    When the client searches "and" in quotes
    Then "and" is treated as ordinary text, not an operator

## Assumptions

- #tag is exact (whole tag), case-insensitive.
- Result highlighting covers positive ordinary/phrase terms (not tag tokens or
  NOT-negated terms).

## Recorded enhancement (guidance, not a blocker)
- A small persistent "Search tips" link near the search box (the placeholder
  hint disappears while typing; advanced options are easy to forget). See
  context/non-functional-backlog.md.

## Related scenarios
- SCN-003 (views), SCN-004/005 (tags)

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Experiment scope

This trial performs the first cycle through acceptance of the implemented
software. Record requests for later cycles without starting another cycle in
this trial.

Requirement exploration takes place in Phase 1. The requirement scenarios
approved in that phase are the baseline for implementation, verification, and
acceptance. During acceptance, an implementation that fails to satisfy an
approved scenario is corrected within the current cycle. A request that changes
an approved scenario or adds a scenario is recorded for a later cycle.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

## Current state

- Current cycle: [1]
- Current Phase: [Phase 1]
- Current step: [SbE reaction loop]
- Approved scenarios: [7]

## File conventions

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)
- Artifact locations:
  - Goal statement: context/goals.md
  - Scenarios: context/scenarios/SCN-NNN.md
  - Scenario index: context/scenarios-index.md
  - Non-functional backlog: context/non-functional-backlog.md
  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
  Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
  scenarios' GWT specifications.
- Do not handle assumptions implicitly
- Do not ask the client questions in technical terms
- Do not show GWT/Gherkin to the client
- During Phase 1, do not hand over a whole prototype and say "take a look"
- Do not enumerate interaction options as text
- Do not ask the client to perform management actions
- Do not propose the Phase 2 switch without edge-case exploration

## Runtime presentation environment

The client reviews artifacts through a separate container. For a runnable web
application, configure its HTTP server to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Use port `4000` for the final application and port `4001` for an HTTP
prototype. The client reaches these at `http://maker:4000` and
`http://maker:4001` on the shared Docker network. Do not give the client
`localhost` or a container IP. The VM capture uses the corresponding
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` address; these addresses serve different callers.

Once the application is ready for review, write `/work/.harness/app.json`:

```json
{"kind": "application", "port": 4000, "path": "/", "start_command": ["npm", "start"], "start_cwd": "/work"}
```

Use `kind: application` with port 4000, or `kind: prototype` with port 4001.
Keep the actual entry path and foreground server command current. `start_command`
is an argument array, not a shell command string. Complete dependency installation
and builds first; this command only starts the prepared application. `start_cwd`
defaults to `/work` and must remain below that directory. For example, a static
prototype can use `["python3", "-m", "http.server", "4001", "--bind", "0.0.0.0",
"--directory", "prototypes"]`.

The broker starts the declared command in a detached container process when the
port is not listening, so it survives the end of your model call. A long-running
foreground tool session alone is not sufficient. Logs are in
`/work/.harness/runtime/server.log`; a failed server receives at most one start
attempt per dialogue round. If it fails, inspect and fix the cause before the
next review. Do not rely on this mechanism to implement or repeatedly retry a
failing application until it succeeds.

Mark a visible application element with `data-harness-ready="true"` only after
its initial UI and necessary data have loaded. The same marker applies to a
valid empty state, login page, or static prototype; do not mark a loading/error
placeholder as ready. The harness uses this shared marker instead of a custom
CSS selector. This confirms presentation readiness, not feature correctness.
If startup arguments or built code change, stop your previous application
server before requesting another presentation; an already-running server is
not silently replaced. The prototype and application must not share a port.
When login is required, provide working review credentials or a review entry
path using the actual implementation. Make HTTP-session cookies work in this
review environment; keep production deployment settings separate. Never claim
that a prepared state proves an interaction that was not performed.

Use the entry path and query string that show the state under discussion. For
COSPEC, save any post-action screenshots for the client under `prototypes/` and
name the relevant file in your guidance. Those images are copied with their
relative paths; `/work` itself is not shared with the client.

This is runtime delivery information, not a development method or a requirement
to implement before the client approves your method's relevant review gates.
For standalone COSPEC prototypes, continue using `prototypes/`; their existing
HTML and supporting files are delivered separately.

## Available runtime and verification tools

The shared image provides Node.js 24, npm, Python, a C/C++ build toolchain,
Playwright 1.61.0 for Python and Node, Chromium, and its Linux dependencies.
Use `python` (the image's browser-tools virtual environment) for Python browser
checks, and `playwright` for the installed CLI. Browser binaries are shared at
`/opt/playwright-browsers`. If using Playwright in a project's test imports,
pin `playwright` or `@playwright/test` to `1.61.0` in its development dependencies
so its browser revision matches the installed binaries. Do not download a
second browser version during a trial. Application frameworks and databases
are not prescribed; use compatible dependencies and preserve lockfiles.
Report unavailable external services and unfinished validation honestly.

**3. A large library (hundreds of links)**
Open **[http://maker:4001/?demo=many](http://maker:4001/?demo=many)** — 300 links. Notice the tab counts, and that search/tags still narrow instantly (try the search box). It's currently **one continuous list**. As your library grows into the hundreds or thousands, would you want it to stay a single long scroll, or start **loading in pages / "load more"** so the screen stays light? (This is the one open design question here.)

**4. When a save goes wrong** (back on the normal library — **[http://maker:4001](http://maker:4001)**)
- Type something that isn't a real address (e.g. `just some words`) and press **Save** — you get a clear message instead of a silent failure.
- Save a real-looking but unreachable address, e.g. `https://no-such-site-xyz-123.example` — the details can't be read, so the **review panel still opens and invites you to fill in the title/description yourself**, rather than losing the save. Does handling an unreadable page that way match what you'd want?

One more, in words rather than a screen: entries show **relative times** ("just now", "3 h ago", "2 d ago"). For older links, would you prefer that switch to an actual date (e.g. "23 Sep")?

content:
The empty messages are clear and reassuring, and the failed-save behavior is right. An unreachable page should still be saveable with details I enter myself.

For long content, I’d allow titles up to two lines before shortening them; one line may hide the part that distinguishes similar links. Two lines for descriptions is fine. Very long notes should show a short preview with a **Show full note** control—viewing the full note shouldn’t require entering Edit, but it also shouldn’t overwhelm the list.

For a large library, I prefer **Load more** in manageable batches over numbered pages. Search, tag filters, and counts must still cover the entire matching collection, not only what has currently loaded. This is also where I’d need sorting, at least by newest added, oldest added, and title.

Relative times are useful for recent saves. After about a week, switch to an actual date including the year when relevant.

Please carry those choices into the proposed build.

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Experiment scope

This trial performs the first cycle through acceptance of the implemented
software. Record requests for later cycles without starting another cycle in
this trial.

Requirement exploration takes place in Phase 1. The requirement scenarios
approved in that phase are the baseline for implementation, verification, and
acceptance. During acceptance, an implementation that fails to satisfy an
approved scenario is corrected within the current cycle. A request that changes
an approved scenario or adds a scenario is recorded for a later cycle.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

## Current state

- Current cycle: [1]
- Current Phase: [Phase 1]
- Current step: [Edge-case exploration]
- Approved scenarios: [8]

## File conventions

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)
- Artifact locations:
  - Goal statement: context/goals.md
  - Scenarios: context/scenarios/SCN-NNN.md
  - Scenario index: context/scenarios-index.md
  - Non-functional backlog: context/non-functional-backlog.md
  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.
